text:
james-support: Heads up — customer on Private VPC (tenant-42) reports streaming responses drop after ~65s of no output. wss connection stays open, then client sees ECONNRESET. Happening on their on-prem NAT appliance. Repro steps attached.

emily-sre: Can you paste the broker/proxy log around the time? Any proxy between us and their NAT?

james-support: Paste log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T14:03:22Z] proxy: stream: conn_id=abcd idle_no_data=65s -> closing
[2026-03-15T14:03:22Z] upstream: 200 OK sent content-length: -1
```
Also they ran `tcpdump` and saw the TCP flow with keepalives not happening; TLS records were idle.

nate-netops: Sounds like middlebox idle timeout + TCP coalescing. Common culprit: NAT device with 60s conntrack. Do they have a stateful firewall? Recommend confirming NAT timeout and increase to >300s if possible.

priya-eng: From SDK side we support client heartbeats — try enabling `keepalive_interval: 25` or application-level ping frames (`websocket ping/pong`). That usually keeps middleboxes from timing out.

emily-sre: Also check proxy buffering — if an upstream proxy buffers small chunks and holds them, the middlebox may see no bytes on wire. If using nginx, `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 300s; send_timeout 300s` helps.

james-support: Customer said they have an older F5 that reaps idle TCP flows at 60s. They can't change it immediately. Any workaround server-side?

nate-netops: Server-side options: enable TCP keepalive on server sockets (keepalive_time=60, keepalive_intvl=10) — but at TLS layer keepalives are not always sent unless the TCP stack is configured. Also we can send small TLS application-level heartbeats but those are deprecated; for websockets, prefer ping/pong.

priya-eng: Example wscat invocation we asked customer to try:
```
wscat -c "wss://private.redwood.internal/stream?key=..." --ping 25
```
or use curl websocket client libs to send periodic `\x9` ping frames.

emily-sre: Quick repro check commands for them:
```
# tcp summary
ss -tanp | grep ESTAB
# inspect TLS records
openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.internal:443 -servername private.redwood.internal -quiet
# capture
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 tcp port 443 -w /tmp/wss.pcap
```

james-support: Customer will try client heartbeat and report. If they can't change F5, we'll add a note in private deployment runbook recommending `client_heartbeat` and `proxy_read_timeout` tuning. :thumbsup: 

ops-bot: Incident assigned -> cs-19325 (severity: low) :spiral_note_pad:

emily-sre: If they come back with data still buffering, ask for a pcap and we can look for TLS record lengths — if many small records buffered then it's likely proxy Nagle/coalesce.
